coverage: Fourteen enumerated sensitive key patterns, case variants and deep object/array traversal.
Authentication keys in JSON response bodies and twice-embedded JSON strings.
Synthetic bearer, JWT-shaped and Viewer-cookie value patterns, including a malformed JSON-shaped string containing a guarded value.
Safe non-authentication inputs, no input mutation, depth64 boundary, wide node budget and cyclic-input refusal.
Independently constructed synthetic67-event chain and known SHA256 test vector.
Exact event count, ordered filename, schema, numeric sequence, intent and preceding raw-byte link.
Middle and final content tamper, whitespace-only raw tamper, malformed event JSON, final SHA, total bytes, intent SHA, record ordering and directory/path identity pins.
Existing source/target isolation and verified-target-only retirement profile guards.
limitations: Every journal, request, credential-shaped string and auth pattern used by these controls is synthetic. No actual private provenance file or retained event was read.
The enumerated secret guards are tested; this is not a comprehensive classifier or proof that arbitrary input contains no secret.

Pure chain validation is tested against trusted synthetic receipt pins. Actual retained67-event bytes, file copying, adjunct sealing, backup-manifest linkage and runtime ownership remain for the parent-controlled operational execution.
No actual PostgreSQL, Docker, HTTP, browser, backup, restore, retirement or source-runtime operation was performed.
acceptance: Focused source controls only; no operational recovery, engineering, native parity or human acceptance claim.
